residence_back_projection.note: A LATER HOME ADDRESS, READ BACKWARDS 8 YEARS. The street is not an 1835 reading: Fergus's Chicago directory of 1843 printed where this person lived in 1843, and this pass carries it back to the scene date because nothing in the 1835 corpus says where the house stood. What is claimed is the street FACE and nothing narrower — no lot, no roof, no door count, and no corner even where the volume prints one — and the grade is `reconstructed`, this dataset's word for a figure the reconstruction supplies rather than a source. Washington Street stands in 1835 under that name and in that place, and the entry prints it as this person's home. The volume narrows it further — it names La Salle Street — and clause R5 declines to take the point: a corner or a run between two crossings is a fact about the numbered grid of the 1840s, and a house moves more than a shopfront does. So the placement is the FACE and nothing narrower, and no roof is dealt. A home is carried back on a weaker argument than a shop is: a shopfront is capital sunk into one street's trade and a lodging is a month's rent, which is why this policy claims less than docs/ADDRESS-BACK-PROJECTION.md does from the same volume. The rule is docs/RESIDENCE-BACK-PROJECTION.md and the liberty is L223; a reader who thinks 8 years is too far to carry a house should read the grade as the disagreement being invited.
